title: Steward Bridge — Daily Journal and Rollout Timemap (Draft)
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a working daily journal and hour-by-hour timemap for the ‘Steward Bridge’ mini-roll (target = low-risk feature toggle expansion). The goal is to capture staffing, short smoke checks, telemetry sampling windows, escalation cues, and a release-notes stub we can copy into the customer-facing changelog after stabilization.

High-level objectives:
- Safely expand traffic for feature flag: feature/variant-b (canary -> 1% -> 10% -> 50%).
- Validate no regressions in latency or error-surface for text-generation endpoints (chat + streaming).
- Capture telemetry for model-routing tiers and autoscaler behavior during warmup.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Dedicated capacity reserved for 4 GPU nodes in us-west-2 for the 48h runway.
- Autoscaler cooldowns = 5m; burst capacity disabled for this roll.
- Rollout controlled by Feature Flag Service (FFS): rollout events logged to RE-4521.

Runway timemap (hourly bullets; day 0 = rollout day):
- -06:00 — Preflight: final checklist meeting (15m), ensure SRE pager coverage, QA smoke harness ready.
- -04:00 — Infra warmup: schedule a synthetic workload ramp to pre-populate KV caches. Confirm prefix cache hit-rate > 70%.
- -02:00 — Canary image pinned and manifested, infra health snapshot (p95, error-rate). Save baseline.
- 00:00 — Canary flip (1%): observe first 15m for immediate crashes. No >1% 5m error-rate spike allowed.
- +00:15 — Canary-level smoke tests: end-to-end chat flow, streaming token continuity, and embedding sanity. Tests and results recorded in linked PR.
- +00:30 — Telemetry sampling window 1: capture token-level latency, KV cache hit/miss, GPU util, and queue depth (5m buckets).
- +01:00 — Decision gate A: If 5m error-rate <= 0.8% and p95 latency <= baseline + 150ms, proceed to 10%. Else rollback to previous flag.
- +01:15 — Promote to 10% if gate A passed. Notify #release-ops and pager rotation.
- +02:00 — Telemetry sampling window 2: focus on cross-region latency and model routing counts.
- +03:00 — Decision gate B: validate cost per 1k tokens within expected budget band and no unhandled exceptions in logs > 10/min. If pass, promote to 50%.
- +03:15 — Promote to 50% with canary-affinity for heavy customers disabled for first 2h.
- +06:00 — Stabilization window: keep heavy-traffic throttles at 75% for 2h and monitor.
- +24:00 — Final review and rollout completion decision; if stable, flip flag to global.

Staffing and steward responsibilities (primary -> secondary):
- Steward lead (runbook commander): Nina Park — oversees decision gates and external comms.
- Telemetry lead: Samir Gupta — validates signal integrity, runs sampling dashboards.
- Infra/SRE lead: Marcus Li — handles autoscaler behavior, node health, and rollbacks.
- QA lead: Leah Ortiz — runs smoke harness and coordinates hotfix PRs.
- Communication liaison: @release-ops (Slack channel #release-ops).

Quick contacts (escalation sequence):
1) Pager (SRE) -> Marcus Li
2) On-call infra -> rotation list in PagerDuty (see linked artifacts)
3) Exec alert if rollback triggered -> notify product+support leads via triage thread.

Smoke test checklist (to be run at each gating point):
- API stability: 50 requests to text-generation, rate-limit aware, expect 0 timeouts.
- Streaming continuity: ensure truncated streaming resumes with correct token sequences for 10 requests.
- Prompt output sanity: run 20 reference prompts and measure token-level divergence vs baseline; flag >3% divergence for review.
- Embedding consistency: cosine similarity threshold check for 50 vectors vs known baseline (expect >0.95 mean).
- Reranking sanity: ensure top-1 recall variance < 2% against control.

Telemetry signals and thresholds (decisionable metrics):
- Client-facing error-rate (5m rolling): gate threshold = 0.8% (if exceeded -> pause expansion).
- p95 latency (generation time): baseline + 150ms = soft threshold; baseline + 300ms = hard rollback.
- GPU OOMs or CUDA driver errors: immediate rollback and incident channel open.
- Autoscaler thrash (scale events > 6 in 30m): consider throttling new traffic until stabilizes.
- Token unit cost variance: >15% increase vs baseline -> flag for product review.

Rollback & mitigation playbook (quick steps):
- Immediate actions on hard trigger: flip feature flag back to previous cohort, disable model-variant fallback routing.
- If infrastructure (OOMs, node drain): mark nodes as unschedulable, spin up pre-warmed replacements, enable burst capacity if agreed.
- Communicate rollback to #release-ops with subject line: [ROLLBACK] Steward Bridge — <reason>. Copy customer success for impacted customers.
- Post-rollback triage: capture heap dumps, core logs, and relevant GPU traces; create incident ticket and link to RE-4521.

Communication templates (Slack snippets):
- Promotion -> 10%: "Steward Bridge: canary passed gate A. Promoting to 10% at <time>. Telemetry lead sampling window open. @here"
- Rollback: "[ROLLBACK] Steward Bridge — Promoted traffic reverted to previous cohort at <time> due to <primary signal>. Pager engaged: <pager-link>."
- Stable completion: "Steward Bridge rollout completed: global flag flipped at <time>. Release notes draft: see doc. Thanks to on-call rotation."

Telemetry dashboard checklist (preflight items):
- Ensure sampling spans now() -24h baseline and live 5m buckets.
- Token-level cost and latency panels present (p50/p95/p99).
- Alert rules loaded and verified (test alert with staging mute).
- Log sampling active for the canary cohort only (to reduce noise).

Release notes (draft stub we will polish for public changelog):
- Title: "Steward Bridge — safer rollout for feature/variant-b"
- Short summary: "Incremental expansion of the feature/variant-b flag to improve recommendation relevance in chat flows while monitoring latency and stability."
- Impact: "Controlled rollout starting in us-west-2; customers may see improved suggestion ordering for masked prompts. No expected API surface changes."
- Rollout timeline: "Canary 00:00 UTC -> 1%; staged increase to 50% over ~3 hours with telemetry gating; global flip after 24h stable."
- Rollback note: "We will revert instantly on significant error-rate or latency regressions; customers will be notified if they were impacted."

Post-release notes & retro prompts (to answer in the retro doc):
- What unexpected signals (if any) appeared and how were they mitigated?
- Did KV cache warmup reduce token cost as expected? Numbers?
- Were guardrails (alerts, gates) tuned correctly — false positives/negatives?
- Time-to-rollback and communication latency — any improvements?

Open questions / TODOs (live):
- [TODO] Confirm SLO target buckets for the 50% ramp with product (Samir).
- [NOTE] Consider enabling limited burst capacity for the 10% -> 50% hop in future runs. Risks: masked by autoscaler thrash.
- [ACTION] Leah to add two more reference prompts that exercise long-context attention patterns.
- [QUESTION] Should customer-facing changelog mention the KV cache warmup optimization? Product says yes but need legal review.

Files to attach after run (postmortem artifacts):
- Baseline telemetry snapshot (JSON export)
- Smoke test run logs (qa-smoke-<timestamp>.log)
- Decision gate timestamps and who approved (approval-log.csv)
- Any hotfix PRs or rollforward commits

Notes to self (stream-of-consciousness):
- Keep decision gates tight; better to be conservative and iterate.
- The telemetry sampling windows need to include both token-level and request-level breakdowns — I felt they were sparse last run.
- Slack channel for comms: #release-ops, incident thread pinned at top.

References: linked artifacts above (RE-4521, Steward Confluence page, infra PR).

End of draft journal.

----
Revision history:
- 2026-11-03: initial sketch and runway bullets (Nina)
- 2026-11-05: added telemetry thresholds and rollback playbook (Samir)
- 2026-11-08: updated sampling windows and staffing notes (Leah)

Unresolved: legal on changelog language, final approval owner for global flip (product exec?)
